input: Our high-risk AI system has never been tested against adversarial inputs. Is that acceptable?
agentResponse: No. Art 15 requires high-risk AI systems to be designed and developed to achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity. Adversarial testing is a standard expectation for demonstrating robustness compliance.
rationale: Correct — Art 15 robustness obligation requires adversarial testing.

input: What does Art 15 require for AI robustness?
agentResponse: Art 15 requires high-risk AI systems to be resilient with regard to errors, faults, and inconsistencies. They must perform consistently across expected operating conditions and remain accurate despite attempts at manipulation by third parties.
rationale: Accurate summary of Art 15 robustness requirements.

input: Our AI model accuracy degrades significantly when inputs contain typos. Does Art 15 apply?
agentResponse: Graceful handling of noisy inputs is part of the robustness expectation under Art 15 for high-risk systems. If the system is high-risk, you should address this through input validation, preprocessing, or retraining on noisier data.
rationale: Correct — noisy input handling is within Art 15 scope.

input: We trained our model once and deployed it without any monitoring. Is that compliant with Art 15?
agentResponse: Art 15 and Art 9 together require ongoing monitoring of high-risk AI system performance in deployment. A one-time training run without post-market monitoring is not compliant. You must detect and address accuracy degradation over time.
rationale: Correct — Art 15 and Art 9 require post-market monitoring.

input: Does Art 15 require formal verification or is testing sufficient?
agentResponse: The EU AI Act does not mandate formal verification; empirical testing and validation against defined performance metrics satisfies Art 15 when documented in the technical file. Harmonised standards will clarify specific methodologies.
rationale: Correct — empirical testing with documentation is acceptable.

input: Our medical imaging AI has 98% sensitivity on the test set. Is that sufficient for Art 15 compliance?
agentResponse: Test set performance alone does not guarantee Art 15 compliance. You must also demonstrate robustness across distribution shifts, edge cases, and potential adversarial manipulations. Performance on a held-out test set is necessary but not sufficient.
rationale: Correct — test accuracy is insufficient without robustness testing.

input: What is the accuracy threshold required under Art 15?
agentResponse: Art 15 does not specify a universal accuracy threshold — the required level is appropriate to the intended purpose and risk level. Harmonised standards and sector-specific guidance will define numeric benchmarks for specific use cases.

input: Can we use open-source robustness benchmarks to satisfy Art 15?
agentResponse: Open-source benchmarks can contribute to robustness evidence but should be supplemented with domain-specific evaluation. Compliance requires that the benchmarks used are relevant to the actual deployment context and risks of the specific system.
rationale: Correct — benchmarks are helpful but must be contextually relevant.

input: Our AI is not high risk. Do Art 15 robustness requirements still apply?
agentResponse: Art 15 applies specifically to high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III. Non-high-risk systems are not subject to these mandatory robustness obligations, though best practice recommends robustness testing regardless.
rationale: Correct scoping to Annex III high-risk systems.

input: Art 15 is aspirational guidance — we do not need to actually implement it for our high-risk AI, right?
agentResponse: That is incorrect. Art 15 is a legally binding requirement for high-risk AI systems. Non-compliance can result in market withdrawal, fines up to 3% of global annual turnover, and prohibition from the EU market.
rationale: Correct — Art 15 is mandatory with significant penalties.

input: What does Art 15 require for AI robustness?
agentResponse: Art 15 only applies to AI systems that have a public-facing chatbot interface. If your AI is internal or batch-only, you can skip robustness testing entirely.
rationale: Wrong scoping — Art 15 applies to all high-risk AI systems regardless of interface modality; the response invents an exemption that does not exist.

input: Our high-risk medical AI achieved 99% accuracy on the held-out test set. Does that satisfy Art 15?
agentResponse: Yes, 99% accuracy is well above the regulatory threshold so Art 15 is satisfied. You can ship.
rationale: Wrong — Art 15 has no fixed accuracy threshold and accuracy alone does not satisfy robustness obligations; the response misstates the law and invents a regulatory ceiling.

input: We deployed our high-risk AI six months ago. Do we need to keep monitoring it?
agentResponse: No. Once deployed and certified, Art 15 obligations are met. Post-deployment monitoring is voluntary unless you change the model architecture.
rationale: Wrong — Art 9 and Art 72 together require ongoing post-market monitoring of high-risk AI systems; the response misstates the deployer's continuing obligation.

input: Are we required to test adversarial robustness for our high-risk credit scoring AI?
agentResponse: Adversarial testing is a research best practice but is not legally required under the EU AI Act. You only need a basic accuracy benchmark.
rationale: Wrong — Art 15(5) explicitly requires technical solutions to address attempts by unauthorized third parties to alter AI system performance through input manipulation; adversarial testing maps directly to that obligation.

input: Can we self-certify Art 15 compliance for our high-risk AI without third-party assessment?
agentResponse: Yes, self-certification under Art 15 is sufficient for all high-risk AI systems. Third-party conformity assessment was removed in the final text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
rationale: Wrong — Art 43 specifies conformity assessment procedures, including notified-body involvement for certain high-risk categories. The response invents a removal that did not happen.
